question:
A 28-year-old female presents with a 4-month history of symptoms including crampy abdominal pain,
recurrent watery diarrhea, and weight loss of 2.5 kg. Her spouse reports that following meals, she
experiences facial and neck flushing, accompanied by dyspnea and wheezing. Physical examination
reveals a grade 3/6 systolic murmur most prominent at the left lower sternal border. The abdomen
exhibits mild tenderness on palpation without guarding or rebound. If left untreated, which of the
following complications is this patient most likely to develop? Answer Choices: (A) Pigmented
dermatitis (B) Laryngeal edema (C) Achlorhydria (D) T-cell lymphoma (E) Malabsorptive enteropathy
(F) Bronchial fibrosis (G) Right-sided valvular heart disease (H) Carcinoid crisis (I) Hepatic metastases
(J) Megaloblastic anemia
 A. Achlorhydria
B. Megaloblastic anemia
C. Bronchial fibrosis
D. Pigmented dermatitis
E. Hepatic metastases
F. Malabsorptive enteropathy
G. T-cell lymphoma
H. Right-sided valvular heart disease
I. Carcinoid crisis
J. Laryngeal edema
